# Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā (Atk Abh01a)

**ID:** Atk Abh01a
**Section:** Aṭṭhasālinī-aṭṭhakathā (atk-abh01)
**Collection:** Atthakatha-Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā
**Title (English, from literature):** The Expositor
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā*, commonly known as the *Aṭṭhasālinī*, is the commentary on the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the first book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Zhu 2017; Griffiths 1986]. In the Pali commentarial tradition it is attributed to Ācariya Buddhaghosa [Zhu 2017; Hazra 1994]. The commentary provides comprehensive semantic, doctrinal, and narrative expositions of Abhidhamma categories. In its introductory and exegetical sections, it discusses the classification of the Tipiṭaka, defining the term *sutta*, explaining the prefix *abhi-* according to multiple nuances (such as growth, reverence, and distinction), and distinguishing the Vinaya as a teaching of commands (*āṇādesanā*), the Sutta as conventional teaching (*vohāradesanā*), and the Abhidhamma as distinct or ultimate teaching (*paramatthadesanā*) [Hazra 1994]. It also preserves narrative and cosmological traditions, such as recording that the Buddha emitted rays while contemplating the *Paṭṭhāna* during the fourth week after his enlightenment, and providing cosmological descriptions of the universe [Zhu 2017; Huntington 2013]. Elsewhere, it glosses canonical verses, including lines from the *Dhammapada* [Levman 2014].

The Pali text was edited for the Pali Text Society by Edward Müller (1897), and another edition was prepared by P. V. Bapat and R. D. Vadekar (1942) for the Bhandarkar Oriental Series [Masefield 1994; Griffiths 1986]. An English translation was published by Pe Maung Tin under the title *The Expositor* [Zhu 2017; Griffiths 1986].

DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language matches with a score of 10 or above, and the text has no entry in SuttaCentral [DharmaNexus]. Within Pali literature, DharmaNexus records extensive text reuse across 580 texts (71,931 matches), showing the highest overlap with commentarial works including the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā*, *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*, *Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā*, and both volumes of the *Visuddhimagga*, as well as Abhidhamma manuals and subcommentaries such as the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* and *Abhidhammāvatāra-purāṇaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].

**Sources**

- [Zhu 2017] Tianshu Zhu, Buddhas and Bodhisattvas: Emanators and Emanated Beings in Buddhist Art of Gandhara, Central Asia, and China (2017) — Identifies the commentary, its narrative of the Buddha's rays during the fourth week, and lists Müller's PTS edition and Pe Maung Tin's translation The Expositor.
- [Griffiths 1986] Paul J. Griffiths, On Being Mindless: Buddhist Meditation and the Mind-Body Problem (1986) — Cites editions by Müller (PTS, 1897) and Bapat and Vadekar (1942), and notes the standard English translation by Pe Maung Tin.
- [Masefield 1994] Peter Masefield, Divine Revelation in Pali Buddhism (1979, 1994) — Lists the bibliographic reference to Müller's 1897 PTS edition.
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pali Language and Literature (1994) — Details Buddhaghosa's explanations of the terms sutta and abhi- and the three desanās in the Atthasālinī.
- [Huntington 2013] Eric Huntington, Portrait of a Landscape: Depictions of the Meru Cosmos in Buddhist Art & Culture (2013) — Notes the inclusion of cosmological descriptions in the Dhammasaṅgaṇī-aṭṭhakathā.
- [Levman 2014] Bryan Geoffrey Levman, Linguistic Ambiguities, the Transmissional Process, and the Earliest Recoverable Language of Buddhism (2014) — Quotes the commentary's exegesis on Dhp 283.
